text:
### Observed differences

- The three activities A19, A20 and A25 kept their participation essentially unchanged: each appears in roughly 3–4 in 10 traces in both windows (A19 about 39% before and 36% after, A20 about 32% before and 35% after, A25 about 31% before and 32% after), and together they cover essentially every trace, consistent with one of the three being chosen per case. [POS001, POS002, POS003]
- Their placement changed sharply: in the earlier window they sat late in the trace (mean relative position about 0.60–0.61), while in the later window they sit early (about 0.32–0.34). [POS001, POS002, POS003]
- Their outgoing transitions changed: earlier, A19, A20 and A25 each split their transitions roughly half to A28 and half to A32 (for example A19 about 47% to A28 and 48% to A32); in the later window, all three lead almost exclusively to A26 (about 88–94% of transitions). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003]
- Their order relative to A26 and A27 flipped: earlier, A26 and A27 came before A19/A20/A25 in about 31–38 in 100 traces and the reverse never occurred; in the later window, A19/A20/A25 come before A26 and A27 in about 30–36 in 100 traces and the old order has nearly disappeared. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]
- A45 re-targeted: earlier, about 85 in 100 of its outgoing transitions went to A26, directly adjacent in about 86 in 100 cases; in the later window, about 85 in 100 go to A19, A20 or A25 (roughly 29% each) and the gap to A26 is typically two steps (about 82 in 100 cases). [DIR006, LAG007]
- Earlier, A27's outgoing transitions went about 47% directly to A28 and about 51% to one of A19/A20/A25, and A28's went about 50% to A32 and about 47% to one of A19/A20/A25; in the later window, A27 leads to A28 in about 98% of its transitions and A28 to A32 in about 96%. [DIR004, DIR005]
- The remaining chain also became tightly sequenced: A27→A28 pairs are directly adjacent in about 98 in 100 later-window cases (about 48 in 100 before), A28→A32 in about 96 in 100 (about 51 before), and the typical A27→A32 distance shortened from three steps to two. [LAG004, LAG005, LAG006]
- A26, A27 and A28, which occur in every trace in both windows, each shifted slightly later (mean relative position up about 0.02–0.03). [POS004, POS005, POS006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the block of alternative activities A19, A20 and A25 now runs in a different place in the process: in the earlier window the chosen activity ran in the late stage — after A26 and A27, inserted either directly before or directly after A28, and leading on to A28 or A32 — whereas in the later window it runs in the early stage, after A45 and before A26, leading into A26, and the tail is left as a fixed, directly connected chain A27 → A28 → A32. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, POS001, POS002, POS003, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007]

The support is direct and consistent: the order flip with A26 and A27 is relational evidence of reordering, the mean-position drop from about 0.60 to about 0.32 is positional evidence, and the transition changes of A19/A20/A25 and A45 show the new wiring directly; the tail lags tightened exactly as expected if the chosen activity no longer interrupts A27→A28→A32. Because the block's participation stayed stable, this is a relocation of when/where these activities run, not a change in how often they run. Screening also backs the item set as a whole: 25 control-flow items qualified where fewer than 1 (0.38) would be expected if nothing had changed, and every item's difference exceeds about 995 of 1,000 random re-splits of the pooled data. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007]

Limitations: three lag items (A19→A32, A25→A28, A25→A32) rest on only 1–3 after-window observations and were not relied on, and the positional indicator uses event positions rather than clock time, though the relational and transition evidence corroborates the reordering. The main competing explanation the two-window design cannot rule out is that both arrangements already existed as variants in the process and the later window merely captured a shift in which variant dominates. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, POS001, POS002, POS003]
